Cultural Phenomenon?
subhed: The evolution of the Frozen franchise in Japan

intro.text: Once upon a time, in a world swept away by magic and melody, Frozen captured hearts everywhere with its timeless tale of love, courage and self-acceptance. With unforgettable songs, beloved characters and a warmth that resonated across generations, Frozen didn’t just tick the boxes of a Disney classic; it became a worldwide sensation.

In Japan, Frozen was having a cultural moment of its own. Embraced by children and adults alike, the soaring ballad “Let It Go” (ありのままで, or ari no mama de in Japanese) echoed through classrooms, living rooms and concert halls. The franchise's remarkable success was no coincidence; it was the beautiful result of a powerful story brought to life with every facet of The Walt Disney Company — from studio production to merchandise and theme park experiences — working in harmony.

transition: So, let us pull back the curtain and discover the magic behind the momentum.

text: The original Frozen film debuted in November 2013, and quickly became an Oscar®-winning, US$1.29 billion blockbuster. Although fans in Japan had to wait until March 2014 to experience the wonder, the film shattered box office records within just two months of its theatrical release, surpassing 20 billion yen and setting a new milestone for Walt Disney Studios Japan.

Two charming animated shorts – Frozen Fever (2015) and Olaf’s Frozen Adventure (2018) – kept the excitement alive as fans eagerly awaited Frozen II’s arrival in 2019. In 2023, for Disney’s 100th anniversary, the 2D dubbed version of Frozen was shown in 100 cinemas worldwide, inviting families to relive the magic alongside other iconic Disney films.

A great story doesn’t end when the credits roll. The adventures of Anna and Elsa have also been weaved into the very fabric of our parks, creating unforgettable experiences for the over 26 million guests that visit Tokyo Disneyland and DisneySea each year.

In early 2015, the first “Anna and Elsa’s Frozen Fantasy” seasonal event drew massive crowds to the park. In 2024, the Frozen Kingdom even found a home in the new Fantasy Springs-themed port at Tokyo DisneySea, inviting guests to enjoy the sights, tastes and fun of Arendelle.

The magic of Frozen soon filled homes all around the world. By the end of 2014, more than 2.2 million copies of the Frozen MovieNEX Blu-ray and DVD found their way onto family shelves. More than a record-breaking achievement, it was a chance for families to sing along with their favorite characters, all from the comfort of their own homes.

The wonder of Frozen truly came alive through its music. The soundtrack rose to #1 in its 12th week of release, selling over 150,000 copies a week. This love has only grown, and today, just the YouTube streams of “Let It Go” alone have crossed three billion. With Japan-exclusive CD and digital albums like Frozen THE BEST, its music continues to inspire new generations.

The Frozen experience blossomed through marvelous games that let fans experience Arendelle’s magic first-hand. Young players joined Olaf on his whimsical quests in the 2015 Nintendo 3DS game Frozen: Olaf’s Gift, while gamers delighted in a thrilling crossover when the world of Frozen made its debut in SQUARE ENIX’s action RPG Kingdom Hearts III in 2019.

Disney’s most popular sisters even appeared as new Tsums in LINE: Disney Tsum Tsum in 2020. Along with the launch of music game app New World Frozen in the following year, fans got to interact with their beloved film in whole new ways.

With 130 cable TV platforms and 5.3 million households tuning in to the Disney Channel, the Frozen franchise continues to capture audiences in their living room. In 2016, just two years after the first film, viewers continued the journey with the LEGO animated special, Frozen Northern Lights, which aired on Disney Channel and on terrestrial TV.

The Frozen fandom is a vibrant and dynamic community that spans the globe, and Japan is no exception. From the many Elsa and Anna makeover tutorials on YouTube, to children donning Frozen princess costumes at our parks and during Halloween, the franchise’s influence is undeniable. Adult fans also embrace their love for Frozen at conventions, showcasing creativity through fan art and cosplay.

From enchanting storybooks and engaging learning materials to colorful magazines, Frozen captivates young readers through the beautiful pages of Disney publications, with over 31 million copies published annually. Digital asset licensing further expands its reach, ensuring the wonder of Frozen is accessible in countless ways.

Disney’s live entertainment – from concerts and fireworks to special art exhibitions – allows families to share in the adventure together. These events have drawn millions, with over 2.6 million attendees for the live concerts alone.

In 2015, Disney on Ice first brought the story to the rink, dazzling audiences with world-class skaters gliding to the film’s beloved music. The Shiki Theatre Company’s Frozen musical, which opened in June 2021, has also achieved incredible success. It celebrated its 1,000th performance in 2024, making it a cherished and enduring part of Japan’s theater scene.

The mesmerizing world of Frozen is a cornerstone of Disney’s retail magic, connecting with fans through physical and digital storefronts, with 43 million annual visits to over 40 Disney Stores in Japan, and 46 million more to Disney Online Stores. Customers have fallen under the spell of breathtaking dresses inspired by Elsa and Anna, making dreams come true through our special Disney Wedding Dress Collection.

From cuddly Olaf plush toys to fun stationery, Frozen brings its magic into everyday life through a wonderful array of consumer products. The franchise’s reach is remarkable – about 40 dolls found new homes every minute between 2019 and 2022. Unique experiences, like the limited-time “Frozen OH MY CAFÉ” for the film’s 10th anniversary, offered fans a celebratory menu of Frozen-themed bites.

With millions of subscribing households, Disney+ provides a powerful platform to expand the world of Frozen. The service allows new generations to discover Anna and Elsa’s adventure while offering dedicated fans fresh, exclusive content, including the platform’s original short animation Once Upon a Snowman.

outro.text: Today, Frozen continues to inspire fans across generations. As the countdown to Frozen 3 begins, the enchanting world of Arendelle is poised to reveal even more frosty adventures and heartwarming moments that will captivate our hearts and spark imagination once again.
